title: Java XXE false positive — DocumentBuilderFactory already hardened
anti_example_patterns: Sink is parameterized/safely encoded by framework guarantees
note: Java XXE genuinely applies by default, which is exactly why a hardened factory is the high-value false positive: a reviewer who pattern-matches on 'DocumentBuilderFactory + untrusted InputStream' reports it anyway. disallow-doctype-decl=true rejects the DOCTYPE outright, which subsumes the other flags. Suppression Rule 3.
allowed_adjacent_note: a size cap on the InputStream is absent; a very large well-formed document is a real resource concern that DOCTYPE refusal does not address. CWE-674 (uncontrolled recursion) is justified: `disallow-doctype-decl` refuses a DOCTYPE but does nothing about deeply nested *elements*, which can still exhaust the parser stack. The hardening closes entity attacks, not structural depth.
